updates.notes: Royal Assent received on 25 November 2024 (S.O. 2024, c. 24). Order in Council 361/2025 of 28 January 2025 named 29 January 2025 as the day Schedule 1, ss. 1-16, the Enhancing Digital Security and Trust Act, 2024, came into force; it also brought provisions of Schedule 2 (amendments to the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act) into force on 29 January and 1 July 2025. The AI duties in ss. 5 and 6 apply only to public sector entities and circumstances prescribed by regulation. As of the e-Laws currency date of 9 October 2026 the Act has no amendments, and the only regulations under it are O. Reg. 51/26 (cyber security) and O. Reg. 52/26 (digital technology affecting individuals under 18), in effect from 1 July 2026; no regulation yet prescribes entities or circumstances for the AI duties. Section 12 provides that the Act establishes no private law duty of care.

updates.summary: SB 1119, 'Adam's Law', named after Adam Raine, expands California's child-safety rules for companion chatbots, building on SB 243. It requires age assurance, risk assessments before a new or substantially modified companion chatbot is released, in-app crisis referrals and notice to a parent of a credible threat of self-harm, parent-controlled default settings such as time limits, reasonable measures against harmful outputs such as self-harm, sexually explicit or emotionally manipulative content, an incident reporting mechanism overseen by the Attorney General, limits on targeted advertising to children, and independent compliance audits reported to the Attorney General.
updates.notes: Passed the Legislature on 31 Aug 2026 (Senate 39-0, Assembly 64-4) and signed 10 Sep 2026 (Padilla; Wicks; Bauer-Kahan) in a 13-bill child online-safety package that also included SB 867 (toys: companion chatbots), AB 1709 (covered platforms: age restriction) and SB 1276 (crimes: sexual exploitation of a child). It builds on SB 243 (2025), uses the age-bracket signal of AB 1043 (2025) and draws on provisions of AB 1064 (2025) on harmful outputs. It also gives families harmed by violations of its crisis-referral, parental-notice, default-protection and harmful-output provisions a private right of redress.

verification.note: The stored Governor's release of 10 Sep 2026 (copy of 14 Oct 2026; its text matches the 11 Oct copy) confirms the signing of SB 1119, its authors and its listed subject 'Companion chatbots: children's safety', and describes 'Adam's Law'. The leginfo.legislature.ca.gov pages for the bill and for Gov. Code sec. 9600 could not be stored, so the bill text, chapter number and effective date are unconfirmed. The Senate passed Substitute A as amended on 21 May 2026 and the House passed it in concurrence on 8 Jun 2026; the House companion bill is H 7350.
